name: swift-27b-tp2-b70
status: serving recipe, measured; candidate on its own branch gates (see notes.unqualified_gates)

model.name: Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B
model.derivative_note: Swift-specific Hessian GPTQ bake of nine linears; INT8 embedding runtime side file (from the checkpoint's config.json _derivative_of / _derivative_note)

engine.attention_backend: K8/V4 native (libxe2_kv.so), oneDNN prefill, MLP-only W4A8
engine.image_note: docker_argv below ends at the environment; the image tag and the vllm argv follow it in this order: engine.image, then vllm_argv

kv_cache.attention_kv_share: 792 B x 16 full-attention layers = 12,672 B/token/card, i.e. ~15.2 GiB of the 19.34 GiB budget the engine reported at boot ('Available KV cache memory') at the measured pool. The remainder is GDN recurrent state for the other 48 layers plus page padding; the two figures are not expected to reconcile exactly.
kv_cache.note: util 0.95 grows the pool to 1,384,612 tokens (+7.8%) with no measured throughput change; 0.90 is the deliberate house value
kv_cache.fp8_comparison: fp8_e4m3 K+V costs 1,024 B per layer per token, so the K8/V4 layout is 22.7% smaller, equivalently fp8 is 29.3% larger. fp8 is supported on this family (the stock server runs it) and was not A/B'd here.
kv_cache.available_kv_budget_source: engine boot log retained at /tmp/arms/logs/async6.log ('Available KV cache memory: 19.35 GiB'); same log holds 'XPU KV cache size: 1,284,329 tokens'

measured.harness: fixed-shape screen: one 300-token code prompt per request, temperature 0, streamed; decode = tokens / (first-to-last delta), token counts from the server usage block; prefill = prompt_tokens / time-to-first-token on a nonce-salted cold prefix

decode_tok_s_single_stream.note: 3 samples in one boot plus 6 in a second; the pooled median is 120.5

log: /tmp/arms/arms2.jsonl ARM async6 (second boot: 6 single-stream samples and every non-single-stream figure); boot log /tmp/arms/logs/async6.log

cross_check_other_harness.harness: BetterBench 0.6.1, corpus v1.0 (hash e332dceff176d033), greedy, 20 passes/category, config qual-ms4.json
cross_check_other_harness.why_different: different corpus and longer generations than the screen above; also that row ran the launcher default util 0.95, not this recipe's 0.90. Compare the concurrency column only, where they agree (339 vs 328 at four streams).

notes.why_it_fits: the checkpoint is ~18.3 GB (17.1 GiB) of INT4; TP2 puts ~9 GiB of weights on each card (7.47 GiB per rank once the embedding is baked to int8), leaving ~19.3 GiB per card for KV at util 0.90, which is what makes a 262,144-token window affordable on 32 GB parts
rejected_here: VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1: no throughput gain and a smaller pool in both boots (1.26M and 1.19M tokens vs 1.28M)
max-num-batched-tokens 8192/16384: neutral or worse (16384: -2.5% c1, -9% c4 aggregate)
max-num-seqs 8 with capture to 56: -6% at concurrency; the 4-slot/28-capture shape is the right one
CCL_TOPO_P2P_ACCESS, IPC-handle cache, all-gather LL algorithm: measured neutral or worse at decode sizes

recordable peer-to-peer all-reduce kernel (from the 4-card B70 tree): 12% better per collective on that build, needs a patch this image does not carry, and the end-to-end estimate stayed under 2% - estimate only, not re-measured here
notes.unqualified_gates: the branch's own qualification gates still fail on the parent commit: attention rel-L2 1.336e-3 against a 1e-3 screen at 131,072 tokens, and the prefill comparison aborts with DEVICE_LOST. These throughput numbers are valid measurements of this candidate, not a fidelity sign-off.
notes.power_ceiling: at 4 concurrent streams the pair draws ~498 W (~250 W/card) against a 275 W firmware cap the driver refuses to raise, which is why most config changes land inside the noise at concurrency
notes.launcher: the argv/env above was produced by tools/launch_tp2_cp2.py (--layout tp2 --graphs --utilization 0.90) and driven by qual-build/run_arm.sh; both live in the qualification fork of this branch, not in this directory. The docker argv and env below are the authoritative reproduction input.
notes.port_provenance: the driver defaults to port 8200; this run was invoked as B70_PORT=19622 B70_BIND=0.0.0.0 B70_UTIL=0.90 bash qual-build/run_arm.sh tp2 --mtp --graphs

provenance.config_matrix: docs/2026-10-21-config-matrix.md in the qualification fork (eight arms, alternating boots)
provenance.collective_measurements: docs/2026-10-21-collective-flags.md in the qualification fork (2-rank oneCCL probe, cards 2-3)
provenance.boot_log_fields: kv_cache_dtype=int8_k_int4_v, async_scheduling=True, gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, cudagraph_capture_sizes=[7,14,21,28], 'XPU KV cache size: 1,284,329 tokens'
provenance.power_source: hwmon energy1_input deltas over the 4-stream window, both cards

hardware.gpus: 2 of 4 Intel Arc Pro B70 (BMG-G31), 32 GB each; this lane leaves cards 2-3 idle
hardware.pcie: Gen4 x16 negotiated end to end: the root port and the switch uplink are Gen4 (max 16 GT/s), the card-facing downstream ports are Gen5-capable but negotiate 16 GT/s. No Xe Link on BMG-G31.
hardware.note: the lane does not depend on peer DMA: topo-P2P collectives measured neutral at its decode sizes, so it runs plain oneCCL with the ring algorithm
